suffixes: The suffix names the signal path, written L>A in the manual and L)A on the display: the letter before the arrow is the input (L = left, R = right, L+R = both inputs averaged) and the letters after it are the outputs A-D it feeds, e.g. L)AD = left input to outputs A and D. A bare L or R is the input half the slider acts on, and LR means one slider shared by both halves of a Split program.
suffixes_source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 4.23 (PDF p. 51), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53), p. 4.28 (PDF p. 56), p. 4.35 (PDF p. 63)

LF DECAY.help: Reverb time (RT60) of the low frequencies, below the Crossover frequency.
LF DECAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.9 (PDF p. 24)

MID DECAY.help: Reverb time (RT60) of the mid frequencies, above the Crossover frequency.
MID DECAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.9 (PDF p. 24)

CROSSOVER.help: The frequency where the low-frequency decay time hands over to the mid decay time. Has no audible effect when the two decay times are equal.
CROSSOVER.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.9 (PDF p. 24); UA Lexicon 224 plug-in manual, Crossover

TREBLE DECAY.help: The frequency above which sound decays progressively faster; lower settings give a darker reverb. The manual recommends 6-10 kHz for a natural hall.
TREBLE DECAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 3.9 (PDF p. 24); UA Lexicon 224 plug-in manual, Treble Decay

DEPTH.help: The listener's apparent position in the space: low = near the stage (mostly early reflections), high = at the back (mostly rear-wall reflections). On the 224X/XL it is on the Hall and Room programs, and in the Halls it affects outputs A and C only.
DEPTH.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.10 (PDF p. 25), p. 4.2 (PDF p. 30); UA Lexicon 224 plug-in manual, Depth

PREDELAY.help: Time from the input to the onset of the reverberation; a longer predelay places the reverb behind the source and suggests a larger space.
PREDELAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.10 (PDF p. 25); UA Lexicon 224 plug-in manual, Predelay

ATTACK.help: Level of the initial sonic pulse (first 50 ms only): high settings give an explosive start, low settings let the sound build up slowly. Plate and Chamber programs only.
ATTACK.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.10 (PDF p. 25)

LF STOP DECAY.help: Low-frequency decay time used in the pauses after the input stops. Active only when the Dynamic Decay toggle is on.
LF STOP DECAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.9 (PDF p. 24), p. 3.10 (PDF p. 25), p. 3.12 (PDF p. 27)

MID STOP DECAY.help: Mid-frequency decay time used in the pauses after the input stops. Active only when the Dynamic Decay toggle is on.
MID STOP DECAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.9 (PDF p. 24), p. 3.10 (PDF p. 25), p. 3.12 (PDF p. 27)

CHORUS.help: Randomly modulates the reverb delays, making the reverb less metallic; higher values raise the modulation rate and pitch wobble. Needs the Mode Enhancement toggle on; in Chorus & Echo it sets the random delay variation of the voices.
CHORUS.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.10 (PDF p. 25), p. 3.12 (PDF p. 27), p. 4.23 (PDF p. 51)

HF BANDWIDTH.help: Corner of a 6 dB/octave low-pass filter at the input, affecting the preechoes and the reverb. It does not change how fast highs decay (that is Treble Decay).
HF BANDWIDTH.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.11 (PDF p. 26)

DIFFUSION.help: How much the echo density builds up at first: high = dense quickly (good for percussion), low = discrete, grainy early echoes (good for vocals).
DIFFUSION.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.11 (PDF p. 26); UA Lexicon 224 plug-in manual, Reverb Diffusion

DEFINITION.help: Echo density in the later part of the decay: at the bottom the program's own rate; raising it thins the tail into distinct repeating echoes.
DEFINITION.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.11 (PDF p. 26)

PREECHO LEVEL.help: Level of one early echo (preecho), a reflection from one wall; 00 = off.
PREECHO LEVEL.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 3.11 (PDF p. 26), p. 3.12 (PDF p. 27)

PREECHO DELAY.help: Delay time of one early echo (preecho). Matching times on a left/right pair keeps the image centred; differences beyond about 2 ms pull it to one side.
PREECHO DELAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 3.11 (PDF p. 26), p. 3.12 (PDF p. 27)

FINE PREDELAY.help: Fine adjustment of the predelay separately for the left and right channels, to tune the stereo image of the reverb.
FINE PREDELAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.10 (PDF p. 25)

SIZE.help: Apparent size of the space, roughly its longest dimension in meters; the range depends on the program, and large sizes limit the available predelay. In Inverse Room it sets when the sound cuts off.
SIZE.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 3.12 (PDF p. 27), p. 4.16 (PDF p. 44)

REVERB STOP DELAY.help: The Gate control: delay before switching from the running decay to the stopped decay. Active only with the Dynamic Decay toggle on; used for gated-reverb effects.
REVERB STOP DELAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.7 (PDF p. 22), p. 3.12 (PDF p. 27), p. 4.22 (PDF p. 50)

SLOPE.help: Inverse Room envelope: below 50 the reverb falls off before the cutoff, at 50 it holds constant level (level slope), above 50 it grows until the cutoff (inverse reverb).
SLOPE.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.16 (PDF p. 44)

VOICE LEVEL.help: Level of one voice (delay tap) in the chorus; 00 = off.
VOICE LEVEL.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.23 (PDF p. 51)

VOICE DELAY.help: Delay time of one voice, i.e. how long before that voice appears at the output.
VOICE DELAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.23 (PDF p. 51)

FEEDBACK.help: Gain of the feedback that recirculates a voice or delay, which sets how long it repeats. Zero-centre: positive feedback above the middle, negative below. In Multiband Delay, sliders 1 and 2 feed their delays back to the input.
FEEDBACK.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.23 (PDF p. 51), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53)

PAN.help: Places the voice, note or band between the outputs: bottom = outputs C and B, top = outputs A and D (Plate/Chorus: 0 = B, 99 = D).
PAN.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.23 (PDF p. 51), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53), p. 4.33 (PDF p. 61)

NOTE LEVEL.help: Level (strength) of one resonant note in Resonant Chords.
NOTE LEVEL.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53)

NOTE PITCH.help: Tunes one resonant note by its loop delay: a shorter delay gives a higher pitch, so the pitch goes down as the slider goes up.
NOTE PITCH.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53)

RESONANCE.help: Feedback for one note's delay line, setting how long it rings. Zero-centre: positive gives all harmonics, negative only odd harmonics; most of the action is in the last 20% of travel.
RESONANCE.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53)

NOTE PREDELAY.help: Delay before one note sounds; staggering the notes turns a pulse into a strum.
NOTE PREDELAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53)

CROSSFEED.help: Level and balance of the feedback mix from predelays 3 and 6 routed back into the left and right inputs of Resonant Chords.
CROSSFEED.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53)

HF CUTOFF.help: Cutoff of a 6 dB/octave low-pass filter: per band in Multiband Delay; in Resonant Chords it limits the highs of the left or right recirculation.
HF CUTOFF.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53)

LF CUTOFF.help: Cutoff of a 6 dB/octave high-pass filter on one band of the Multiband Delay.
LF CUTOFF.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53)

BAND LEVEL.help: Relative level of one band of the Multiband Delay (the input is the average of L and R).
BAND LEVEL.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53)

BAND DELAY.help: Delay time of one band of the Multiband Delay: short for slap echoes, long for layering.
BAND DELAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53)

LEVEL.help: On a preecho page: the level of one early echo. In Chorus & Echo and Plate/Chorus: a voice level; in Resonant Chords: a note level; in Multiband Delay (L+R): a band level.
LEVEL.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.23 (PDF p. 51), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53), p. 4.27 (PDF p. 55)

DELAY.help: On a preecho page: the delay of one early echo. In Resonant Chords (no output suffix): the note predelay, the time before that note sounds.
DELAY.source: 224X owner's manual v8.2 p. 3.8 (PDF p. 23), p. 4.25 (PDF p. 53), p. 4.26 (PDF p. 54)

INACTIVE.help: This slider has no function on this page.

BASS.help: Original 224: reverb decay time of the frequencies below the Crossover (0.6 to 70 s).

MID.help: Original 224: reverb decay time of all frequencies above the Crossover (0.6 to 70 s), not only the midrange.
